source.title: VISTA: A Panoramic View of Neural Representations

page_placements.theme: Residual polysemanticity and context-dependent feature explanations

record.tranche_reason: Uses a different method—visual inspection of SAE-latent activation maps—to examine whether features in a language model have interpretable structure. It does not test toy-model superposition.
record.gate_note: The paper reports semantic patterns for three Gemma2-2B SAE latents, which bear on the indirect-evidence version. Mutual-knn gain values measure fidelity of the VISTA maps, not feature recovery or superposition, so they are not rows.
record.test_reason: This is a visualization-tool paper. It takes Gemma Scope SAE latents as given and asks whether its VISTA maps agree with the automated labels for three latents. It does not test whether features are superposed, whether an SAE recovers real features, or whether SAE latents are canonical units. Its results measure the labels and the tool, not the claim.
record.authors_conclusion: Correct: the authors present VISTA as a complementary tool that confirms some automated SAE-latent labels and reveals secondary or unexpected patterns those labels miss.
record.recipe_differences: Uses SAE-latent activation maps, UMAP, and text-to-image visualizations; it does not use the original toy-network superposition method.
record.method_sensitivity: The authors report stable clustering across runs with different random seeds, but say the intended stretching along the latent axis was not always achieved.

fits_no_version.finding: For Gemma2-2B Gemma Scope layer-20 SAE latents, visual inspection of top-activating captions found patterns that the automated labels miss. Latent 9745 has a secondary trigger on M-initial words (about 40% of top inputs). Latent 9220 fires on 'X or Y' conjunctions rather than financial obligation.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Automated LLM labels of SAE latents can be incomplete or wrong, and individual SAE latents can carry mixed (semantic plus morphological) triggers.

record.peer_reviewed: 38th Conference on Neural Information Processing Systems (NeurIPS 2024)
record.problems: Only three latents are examined in the case studies, all from one model and layer. The analysis relies on visual inspection and has no stated ground-truth feature-recovery evaluation or controls. The authors note possible dataset domain skew and limitations of automated interpretation.
record.rows_left_out: Mutual-knn gain results for the three maps are omitted because they measure visualization-map fidelity rather than SAE feature recovery or superposition (Sections 3.2.1–3.2.3; Appendix A).

untested.parts: All: no toy models, geometry or sparsity transition.
Does not test feature spread across neurons or SAE feature recovery; uses pretrained Gemma Scope SAEs as a given.
No completeness, stability or canonicality test. It has three anecdotal latents whose meanings differ from their automated labels.
All: no test of feature dimensionality.

record.verdict_notes: The reader's 'tests'/T2 classification and its V4 labels are rejected. Labelling an SAE latent as interpretable says nothing about whether real models contain recoverable sparse features or superposition. The evidence is three hand-picked latents from one SAE, inspected on an out-of-domain image-caption dataset, with no controls. The mutual-knn gain values measure map fidelity and are rightly left out.

versions.untested_parts: Toy networks, feature overlap and geometry, and sparsity-dependent transitions.
Whether capacity pressure explains polysemanticity or causes important features to get dedicated dimensions.
Whether polysemantic neurons arise without capacity pressure.
Does not establish ground-truth feature recovery, features spread across neurons, or generalize beyond the three examined latents and this model.
Completeness, stability, and canonical status of SAE features.
Whether represented features are one-dimensional directions rather than multidimensional.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2B SAE 16k residual layer 20
rows.operation_detail: Visually inspected the VISTA map for SAE latent 20-5011 using captions with high latent activation.

conditions.value: top 4000 (2%) of 200,000 auto-generated short captions maximizing the latent

rows.measure: Semantic patterns in the latent activation map
rows.baseline: Gemma Scope label: ingredients and dishes related to food preparation and recipes
rows.value: Visual inspection confirmed many food-related ingredients, including champagne, beer, iced tea, chips, honey, pizza, pretzels, and cheese.
rows.note: The authors report that the visual patterns support the automated label.
rows.check: Compares the VISTA map with Gemma Scope's automated label for one latent. This checks label accuracy and tool output, not whether a dictionary recovers sparse features (V4). The data are the top 2% of activating image captions, which is a selection set, not a test of feature recovery.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2B SAE 16k residual layer 20
rows.operation_detail: Visually inspected the VISTA map for SAE latent 20-9745 using captions with high latent activation.

conditions.value: top 4000 (2%) of 200,000 auto-generated short captions maximizing the latent

rows.measure: Semantic patterns in the latent activation map
rows.baseline: Gemma Scope label: references to muscle-related subjects and terminology
rows.value: The map showed muscular imagery, but about 40% of inputs lacked muscular references and instead clustered around words beginning with M.
rows.note: The authors describe the M-word pattern as a weak additional trigger.
rows.check: Label-agreement observation, not a measure of any version. The finding is a secondary trigger: about 40% of top inputs cluster on M-initial words. This could hint at a mixed-meaning SAE latent, but there is no control or stability test, so it does not bear on V5. Recorded under fits_no_version.

rows.subject: Gemma2-2B SAE 16k residual layer 20
rows.operation_detail: Visually inspected the VISTA map for SAE latent 20-9220 using captions with high latent activation.

conditions.value: top 4000 (2%) of 200,000 auto-generated short captions maximizing the latent

rows.measure: Semantic patterns in the latent activation map
rows.baseline: Gemma Scope label: expressions related to legal or financial obligations
rows.value: The map showed clear visual clusters with no finance references; the authors identified clusters involving animal combinations, sky combinations, and style combinations.
rows.note: The authors suggest domain skew or limitations of automated techniques could explain the discrepancy with the label.
rows.check: 'partial' misstates the result. The authors call this the most divergent case: there are no finance references, and the latent fires on 'X or Y' visual conjunctions. The out-of-domain caption dataset may explain this, as the authors note. It is not a measure of any version.

source_check.scope: Only the listed rows, labels and statements were checked; presence is not whole-study approval.

relation.reason: Takes SAE latents as inputs to VISTA without testing superposition, feature recovery, completeness, stability, canonicality, or feature dimensionality.

tranche.reason: Uses existing Gemma Scope SAE representations to demonstrate a visualization method and compare visual interpretations with automated labels; it does not test any stated superposition claim version.

source_check.notes: The authors-conclusion paraphrase is accurate. The synthesis statement's approximately 40% finding is supported by R2; R3 concerns a different latent and supplies no evidence for that percentage. Row values and baselines are truncated in the check pack; their visible portions agree with the text.

reader_labels.label: supports
reader_labels.reason: The map showed numerous food-related patterns consistent with an interpretable SAE latent (R1).

reader_labels.label: limits_scope
reader_labels.reason: The maps included substantial patterns not captured by their automated labels, showing that latent interpretations may be mixed or differ from the supplied label (R2, R3).
